Ships cross Panama by climbing a staircase of water. 🚢 Watch the canal's locks get built in 17 seconds. ⏱️

France tried first and failed. When the US took over in 1904, step one was beating the mosquitoes that spread yellow fever and malaria. Then: cut through the mountains, dam the Chagres River, and pour giant concrete lock chambers, each one 320 m long.

The twist: the canal doesn't cut through at sea level. Ships float into a chamber, it fills with water, and they rise step by step about 26 m up to Gatun Lake, sail across, then step back down to the other ocean.

Would you rather sail through it or watch from the side? 👇

yt_description:
After the French attempt failed in the 1880s, the US took over on 4 May 1904. Gorgas' mosquito campaign nearly eliminated yellow fever and malaria; the Culebra Cut sliced through the continental divide; damming the Chagres created Gatun Lake ~26 m (85 ft) above sea level. Three locks lift ships 85 ft; each lock is 320 m long and 33.5 m wide. Opened 15 Aug 1914 (SS Ancon). About 5,600 workers died during the US phase.

Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panama_Canal · https://www.history.com/articles/panama-canal
Figures are historical estimates. Stylised 3D animation.
